Everything we make, in one list. Pick a style and go.

FontGen is deliberately small — a focused set of text and font generators, each one done properly, rather than a sprawl of half-working tools. They all share the same engine: type once, the chosen style updates instantly on the right, copy what you like. Here's the full lineup. (More on the way; we'd rather ship a tool that works than pad the list.)

How the generators are grouped

Under the hood the styles fall into a few families, and the dropdown on each tool groups them the same way:

  • Calligraphic — script, cursive, bold script, blackletter / fraktur, and small caps. The flowing, decorative letterforms. Letters only; no numbers.
  • Weight — bold and italic in their sans and serif variants. The safest set for getting past app font restrictions; bold sans renders almost everywhere.
  • Outline — double-struck and monospace. Clean, technical-looking letterforms with full numbers.
  • Decorative — full-width / aesthetic, circled bubble letters, squared letters, parenthesized, bracketed. The boxed-and-spaced looks.
  • Effect — strikethrough, underline, slashed, zalgo / glitch. These add marks to your existing letters rather than replacing them, so they layer on top of anything.
  • Misc — superscript, subscript, wide-spaced, dotted, upside-down, reversed. The odds and ends, including a couple of joke tools.

Which one should I use?

For a bio or caption, calligraphic and small caps read as the most deliberate. For a username or game tag, stick to Weight (bold) or full-width — they pass the most name filters. For a chat flex, the glitch and circled styles get the most reactions. And if a glyph shows as an empty box somewhere, that's the receiving app's font, not the tool — switch to Bold or Small Caps, which render the widest. There's a full app-by-app compatibility rundown if you want the specifics, and a plain explanation of how the whole Unicode trick works.

Not finding the one you want?

If there's a style you keep needing that isn't here — a specific symbol set, a regional alphabet effect, something — the contact page is open. We add styles based on what people actually ask for, not on keyword lists.
